messages:
maria: heads-up — started a staged deploy (pilot) for runtime v2.3.1 in us-west-2. can someone run a quick perf sanity (p50/p95/p99 + throughput) and check for regressions? trying to decide rollforward vs hold.

luis: on it. i'll run the standard rt-bench for 10m against the pilot pool and post numbers.

matt: FYI deploy-bot stopped at 30% because the auto gate saw p99 > 400ms threshold.

deploy-bot: rollout paused at 30% (automated performance gate tripped: p99=428ms > 400ms). See /ops/runbooks/perf-gates for next steps.

sophie: quick note — traffic shape for the pilot today is heavier on long-seq (avg 820 tokens) than our window, might bias p99. still worth checking.

luis: benchmark run complete (10m, concurrency=16, seq=1024). results: p50=62ms, p95=210ms (+8% vs baseline), p99=428ms (+35% vs baseline). throughput steady ~185 req/s. GPU util 76%, queue length slowly increasing (~12% backlog).

maria: thanks. that p99 jump looks concerning. any signs of KV cache misses or memory thrashing?

matt: initial traces show bursts of extra KV lookup spikes around the same time as p99 tails — could be cache eviction behavior with the new memory allocator in v2.3.1.

anita: can we try flipping the cache TTL back to 30s and re-run? if it's an allocator/regression we should hold and rollback.

luis: can re-run but it will take ~12m to stabilize. suggestion: try a single node with cache_ttl=30s first.

maria: run the quick patch on one pilot node and post updated numbers. use this command:

```
# bench command
./bin/rt-bench --model rwd/13b-qlora --seq 1024 --concurrency 16 --duration 600
# set config via ssm: cache_ttl=30
```

matt: also check gpu kernel timings (nvprof) and look at memcpy spikes — i saw a handful of 4-6ms memcpy events that correlate.

luis: patched one node to cache_ttl=30s and re-ran: p50=60ms, p95=205ms, p99=312ms (now +8% vs baseline). queue backlog cleared. gpu memcpy spikes still present but much rarer.

sophie: dashboard: https://internal.redwood/d/pilot/perf?panelId=9 — compare before/after.

anita: given that flipping TTL reduces tail, i'm leaning toward holding the rollout until we ship a config fix in v2.3.2. what do folks think? vote: +1 hold & rollback to 0% (revert to v2.2) vs -1 proceed but limit to 20% and monitor. please reply with emoji.

matt: +1 (prefer rollback, we don't want regression in prod). :thumbsup:

luis: +1 to hold; will dig into allocator mem patterns. :thumbsup:

sophie: -1 leaning -1 only if we can keep pilot at 20% and autoscale min_replicas=3. otherwise rollback. :thumbsdown:

maria: +1 — safety first. i'll start rollback to v2.2 for the pilot group now and open an incident for tracking.

deploy-bot: starting rollback to v2.2 for rollout group at 30%. estimated completion 3m.

anita: thanks all. action items: luis investigate allocator + memcpy root cause, matt collect kernel profiles, sophie prepare dashboard diff for post-mortem, maria coordinate release notes and incident. we'll re-run a staged deploy after fixes and a small A/B test.

maria: rolling back complete, pilot is back to v2.2. closing this thread; will post follow-ups in eng-runtime. :white_check_mark:
